note:
ISO 2026-W32 runs from August 3 through August 9. Mars is about 1.8° in ecliptic longitude from Elnath in Taurus. Mars and Ceres are separated by about 2.0° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌗 Last Quarter — 02:21:29 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Eltanin as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -11.3; direct motion; 81.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 05:27 UTC. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 05:42 UTC. Conjunction with Saturn in ecliptic longitude Aug 03 23:21 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Aug 07 14:51 UTC. Conjunction with Neptune in ecliptic longitude Aug 03 04:22 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 0.1; direct motion; 41.3% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.3; direct motion; 55.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 93.4% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 05:27 UTC. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 18:06 UTC. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 98.3% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 05:42 UTC. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Aug 09 18:06 UTC. Jupiter: In solar glare; magnitude -1.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.6; retrograde motion; 99.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 03 23:21 UTC. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 07 14:51 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 03 04:22 UTC. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.4; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

story_candidates.dek: Ptolemy's Cluster is an observing target in Sco carried by the weekly Calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Ptolemy's Cluster as one of this week’s fixed-sky observing targets.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Sco constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

story_candidates.dek: Eltanin is a star in Dra; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 17h 56m and declination +51.5°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star is circumpolar (at 45° declination it touches the geometric horizon at lower culmination). It reaches approximately 84° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Dra constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
